facts.fact: NIRA says all CRVS registration systems are under one authority and the NIN is issued automatically once a birth notification is made; it also says push and pull between NSIS and the marriage system is still lacking and death registration is very disconnected.

UGA.note: No count or share of people enrolled is given.

facts.fact: NIRA says the NIN is issued automatically once a birth notification is made and certification is immediate, with no biometrics needed for a child 9 months or under; deploying crvs.nsis.nira.go.ug for birth registration and instant NIN generation is still a next step.
NIRA, the national authority, created NSIS in 2014/15 and developed its birth and death registration module itself, using open source OpenCRVS, keeping core personnel throughout.
NIRA says the birth and death registration module integrated into NSIS uses open source OpenCRVS, and the marriage module is also being built on OpenCRVS.

UGA.note: Marriage registration requires the NIN of the couple, but no electoral, tax, payroll, social or business register is named.

facts.fact: NIRA says registration for and issuance of the National ID and NIN began with the creation of NSIS in 2014/15, and that duplicate and multiple registrations have been reduced.
